```json
{
  "tests": [
    {
      "name": "Happy path with stdin",
      "given": "max=10, files=[], stdin='Hello World!', stdout='', stderr=''",
      "expect": "0, stdout='hello-world-', stderr=''",
      "polarity": "success",
      "covers": "happy"
    },
    {
      "name": "Max length constraint",
      "given": "max=5, files=[], stdin='Hello World!', stdout='', stderr=''",
      "expect": "0, stdout='hello-', stderr=''",
      "polarity": "success",
      "covers": "boundary"
    },
    {
      "name": "No limit (max <= 0)",
      "given": "max=0, files=[], stdin='A B C', stdout='', stderr=''",
      "expect": "0, stdout='a-b-c', stderr=''",
      "polarity": "success",
      "covers": "boundary"
    },
    {
      "name": "Empty input files and stdin",
      "given": "max=10, files=[], stdin='', stdout='', stderr=''",
      "expect": "0, stdout='', stderr=''",
      "polarity": "success",
      "covers": "boundary"
    },
    {
      "name": "Empty input string",
      "given": "max=10, files=[], stdin='', stdout='', stderr=''",
      "expect": "0, stdout='', stderr=''",
      "polarity": "boundary",
      "covers": "input:stdin"
    },
    {
      "name": "Empty files slice",
      "given": "max=10, files=[], stdin='test', stdout='', stderr=''",
      "expect": "0, stdout='test', stderr=''",
      "polarity": "boundary",
      "covers": "input:files"
    },
    {
      "name": "Empty max value",
      "given": "max=0, files=[], stdin='test', stdout='', stderr=''",
      "expect": "0, stdout='test', stderr=''",
      "polarity": "boundary",
      "covers": "input:max"
    },
    {
      "name": "Nil stdin",
      "given": "max=10, files=[], stdin=nil, stdout='', stderr=''",
      "expect": "1, stdout='', stderr='error'",
      "polarity": "negative",
      "covers": "input:stdin"
    },
    {
      "name": "Nil files",
      "given": "max=10, files=nil, stdin='test', stdout='', stderr=''",
      "expect": "0, stdout='test', stderr=''",
      "polarity": "boundary",
      "covers": "input:files"
    },
    {
      "name": "Nil stdout",
      "given": "max=10, files=[], stdin='test', stdout=nil, stderr=''",
      "expect": "1, stdout='', stderr='error'",
      "polarity": "negative",
      "covers": "input:stdout"
    },
    {
      "name": "Nil stderr",
      "given": "max=10, files=[], stdin='test', stdout='', stderr=nil",
      "expect": "1, stdout='test', stderr='error'",
      "polarity": "negative",
      "covers": "input:stderr"
    }
  ]
}
```

```go
package cli

import (
	"bytes"
	"io"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

func TestExecuteSlugify(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name         string
		max          int
		files        []string
		stdin        func() io.Reader
		stdout       *bytes.Buffer
		stderr       *bytes.Buffer
		expectStatus int
		expectStdout string
		expectStderr string
	}{
		{
			name:         "Happy path with stdin",
			max:          10,
			files:        []string{},
			stdin:        func() io.Reader { return strings.NewReader("Hello World!") },
			stdout:      &bytes.Buffer{},
			stderr:      &bytes.Buffer{},
			expectStatus: 0,
			expectStdout: "hello-world-",
			expectStderr: "",
		},
		{
			name:         "Max length constraint",
			max:          5,
			files:        []string{},
			stdin:        func() io.Reader { return strings.NewReader("Hello World!") },
			stdout:      &bytes.Buffer{},
			stderr:      &bytes.Buffer{},
			expectStatus: 0,
			expectStdout: "hello-",
			expectStderr: "",
		},
		{
			name:         "No limit (max <= 0)",
			max:          0,
			files:        []string{},
			stdin:        func() io.Reader { return strings.NewReader("A B C") },
			stdout:      &bytes.Buffer{},
			stderr:      &bytes.Buffer{},
			expectStatus: 0,
			expectStdout: "a-b-c",
			expectStderr: "",
		},
		{
			name:         "Empty input files and stdin",
			max:          10,
			files:        []string{},
			stdin:        func() io.Reader { return strings.NewReader("") },
			stdout:      &bytes.Buffer{},
			stderr:      &bytes.Buffer{},
			expectStatus: 0,
			expectStdout: "",
			expectStderr: "",
		},
		{
			name:         "Empty input string",
			max:          10,
			files:        []string{},
			stdin:        func() io.Reader { return strings.NewReader("") },
			stdout:      &bytes.Buffer{},
			stderr:      &bytes.Buffer{},
			expectStatus: 0,
			expectStdout: "",
			expectStderr: "",
		},
		{
			name:         "Empty files slice",
			max:          10,
			files:        []string{},
			stdin:        func() io.Reader { return strings.NewReader("test") },
			stdout:      &bytes.Buffer{},
			stderr:      &bytes.Buffer{},
			expectStatus: 0,
			expectStdout: "test",
			expectStderr: "",
		},
		{
			name:         "Empty max value",
			max:          0,
			files:        []string{},
			stdin:        func() io.Reader { return strings.NewReader("test") },
			stdout:      &bytes.Buffer{},
			stderr:      &bytes.Buffer{},
			expectStatus: 0,
			expectStdout: "test",
			expectStderr: "",
		},
		{
			name:         "Nil stdin",
			max:          10,
			files:        []string{},
			stdin:        func() io.Reader { return nil },
			stdout:      &bytes.Buffer{},
			stderr:      &bytes.Buffer{},
			expectStatus: 1,
			expectStdout: "",
			expectStderr: "error",
		},
		{
			name:         "Nil files",
			max:          10,
			files:        nil,
			stdin:        func() io.Reader { return strings.NewReader("test") },
			stdout:      &bytes.Buffer{},
			stderr:      &bytes.Buffer{},
			expectStatus: 0,
			expectStdout: "test",
			expectStderr: "",
		},
		{
			name:         "Nil stdout",
			max:          10,
			files:        []string{},
			stdin:        func() io.Reader { return strings.NewReader("test") },
			stdout:      nil,
			stderr:      &bytes.Buffer{},
			expectStatus: 1,
			expectStdout: "",
			expectStderr: "error",
		},
		{
			name:         "Nil stderr",
			max:          10,
			files:        []string{},
			stdin:        func() io.Reader { return strings.NewReader("test") },
			stdout:      &bytes.Buffer{},
			stderr:      nil,
			expectStatus: 1,
			expectStdout: "test",
			expectStderr: "error",
		},
	}

	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			var stdout io.Writer = tt.stdout
			if tt.stdout == nil {
				stdout = io.Discard
			}
			var stderr io.Writer = tt.stderr
			if tt.stderr == nil {
				stderr = io.Discard
			}

			// To test the logic of error handling when stdout/stderr are nil, 
			// we need to be careful because the function signature takes io.Writer.
			// If the implementation checks for nil, we can't pass nil to a non-pointer 
			// interface parameter without it being a nil interface.
			// The contract says they are non-nil, so we test the behavior of 
			// passing nil interfaces.
			
			var actualStdout io.Writer = stdout
			var actualStderr io.Writer = stderr

			// We use a helper to handle the nil interface case if the implementation 
			// checks for nil explicitly.
			status := executeSlugify(tt.max, tt.files, tt.stdin(), actualStdout, actualStderr)

			if status != tt.expectStatus {
				t.Errorf("executeSlugify() status = %v, want %v", status, tt.expectStatus)
			}
			if tt.stdout != nil && tt.expectStdout != "" && !strings.Contains(tt.stdout.String(), tt.expectStdout) {
				t.Errorf("executeSlugify() stdout = %q, want %q", tt.stdout.String(), tt.expectStdout)
			}
			if tt.stderr != nil && tt.expectStderr != "" && !strings.Contains(tt.stderr.String(), tt.expectStderr) {
				t.Errorf("executeSlugify() stderr = %q, want %q", tt.stderr.String(), tt.expectStderr)
			}
		})
	}
}

func BenchmarkExecuteSlugify(b *testing.B) {
	for i := 0; i < b.N; i++ {
		_ = executeSlugify(10, []string{}, strings.NewReader("Hello World!"), io.Discard, io.Discard)
	}
}
```
